ana_ts: Quick PSA — onboarding sample app failing for CJS users on Node 16. Getting `Cannot use import statement outside a module` when they `require('redwood-sdk')`.

tom_sdk: ugh, yeah. We're shipping ESM by default in the sample but not providing a clean CJS fallback in package.json/exports. Also some TypeScript overloads are confusing tsc for older TS configs.

jessica_devex: can you paste the error + the package.json snippet? i want to update the walkthrough.

ana_ts: here's what a user hit: 
```
Error [ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION]: Cannot use import statement outside a module
    at Module._extensions..js (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:1099:13)
    at Object.require (internal/modules/cjs/helpers.js:76:18)
```
And their package.json has "type": "commonjs" and they do `const { createClient } = require('redwood-sdk')`.

liam_eng: two quick notes: (1) Edge runtimes (Vercel/Cloudflare) require ESM and no dynamic require, so our edge builds must be ESM-only; (2) Node 12/14/16 CJS users still exist, so we need conditional exports.

ana_ts: example export mapping that worked for us locally: 
```json
{
  "name": "redwood-sdk",
  "type": "module",
  "main": "dist/cjs/index.js",
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
      "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
    }
  },
  "types": "dist/index.d.ts"
}
```

tom_sdk: yup. conditional exports + shipping both builds fixes runtime import issues. But the TS types also need a single, non-ambiguous signature. We're seeing complaints like: `No overload matches this call` because our overloads and generics are tangled.

jessica_devex: what exactly is the typing problem? can we show a minimal reproducer?

tom_sdk: minimal problem: we currently have two overloads for createClient which differ only by generic presence: 
```ts
function createClient<T>(opts: ClientOpts & { schema?: T }): Client<T>;
function createClient(opts: ClientOpts): Client<any>;
```
When users have `--noImplicitAny` or older TS, inference goes weird and users get `any` or overload isn't selected. Also some consumer tsconfigs use `moduleResolution: node` vs `bundler` and pick different declaration resolution paths.

liam_eng: my recommendation: collapse to a single generic with a default and prefer `unknown` over `any` in public API. Eg: 
```ts
export function createClient<T = unknown>(opts: ClientOpts & { schema?: T }): Client<T>;
```
That keeps inference but forces explicit narrowing on consumer side.

ana_ts: +1. Also add this note to onboarding: "If you use CJS/require, import from the CJS entry: `const { createClient } = require('redwood-sdk/dist/cjs')` — but prefer updating to Node >=16 with ESM to match edge."

jessica_devex: action items: (1) tom: add conditional exports + ensure build outputs at dist/esm & dist/cjs; (2) tom: change d.ts to single-generic signature and publish a patch; (3) jessica: update onboarding sample and add a troubleshooting section for CJS/TS configs; (4) liam: smoke test on Vercel Edge + Node16 CJS container. I'll open a PR template for the doc change.

ci-bot: Build queued for branch: fix/sdk-exports-typing (pipeline #2345) :gear:

tom_sdk: also note: for tsconfig compat, recommend these in docs: 
```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2020",
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true
  }
}
```
Older `moduleResolution: "node"` users may resolve the wrong .d.ts if they rely on `typesVersions` or nonstandard outputs.

liam_eng: last thing — log a short migration note for enterprise customers using Dedicated/private infra. Some internal deploys pin Node12/14 and will need guidance.

jessica_devex: Roger. I'll draft the doc and link the reproducer. Thanks for the quick triage, all.
